help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file that has already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing is started. The service and source shown remain the current ones, and next to the service name a message appears saying where the file will move to, for example Will switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) after resuming. Choosing again replaces this message; choosing the source that is already in use removes it. After you resume the download, the message shows Switching to … until the switch takes effect, after which it disappears. If the paused files of one download would move to different places or the destination is unknown, the destination is not shown. A file that has not yet started downloading has nothing to hand over, so its new source is simply applied when it starts downloading. Choosing a service while paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take the link in use immediately takes the download over (this is visible on the badge), while a service that first needs to prepare a copy shows Preparing: … and takes the download over only after you resume it. These messages appear in the rows of the "Download activity" block and of the "Downloads" page; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.settings.access_integrations.integr.backTranslation: Integration accounts are intended for automation, and they cannot sign in to these pages. Issue token shows the new token only once, so copy it right away; tools send it as {literal}. Each token sees only the jobs sent with it. Revoke stops the token immediately, without affecting anything it has already sent.

Delivery profiles for integrations define, for an external program such as Sonarr or Radarr, which categories it may send downloads to, which source types it may pass (Source types), which of its tokens may use the profile (Allowed API tokens), and where it will find finished files (DP download path in the DebridPulse downloads folder and External import path — the same folder as seen by the program). Files are shared where they lie: nothing is copied, moved or deleted for the program. help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts show each person with their role, sign-in method and account state (enabled or not). Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in the Edit user window takes effect at once: that person's open pages reload with the new role without signing out. Each person has a DebridPulse username separate from the display name: an OIDC account receives it at first sign-in, and a local password is used with exactly this name to sign in; the pencil next to it in the header of the Edit user window changes it, keeping the existing password. Click an account's name to see its details and activity; there you can separately revoke an unfinished request. Disable and Remove first show how many unfinished download requests the account has; these requests are revoked, a transfer that someone else also requested continues, and finished downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sign-in sessions and stops its tokens; removing keeps the account's history and deletes its own notification settings. If a removed OIDC sign-in returns, it gets a new account, which stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into one that you decide to keep; two accounts with a shared verified email address will be flagged, but they can be merged only with the "Merge" action. DebridPulse always keeps at least one working administrator, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.
